source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Record the wound stage and a photograph only; measurements and drainage characteristics can be added at discharge.","B":"Record the dressing type and pain score only because wound-bed and surrounding-skin findings are treatment rather than assessment data.","C":"Delay the baseline description until the first scheduled dressing change so admission findings do not affect later comparisons.","D":"Record the wound’s precise location, size, wound-bed and periwound findings, drainage, pain, and other relevant assessment characteristics."}}
source_row.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills specifies that wound assessment and documentation include anatomical location, wound type, tissue damage, wound bed, size, edges and periwound skin, signs of infection, pain, and drainage characteristics. Accurate baseline documentation supports ongoing comparison and care planning.
source_row.source_detail: Wound assessment documentation includes precise location, size, wound characteristics, periwound findings, drainage, infection findings, and pain. Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: During admission, a nurse identifies a wound on a client's lower leg. Which documentation is most appropriate?
